blocks.x: We’re officially less than a week away from the first day of fall in our favorite city! From our many parks exploding with seas or red, yellow and orange to the smell of pumpkin spice radiating through our local coffee shops, this time of year is magical from start to finish.

And while there’s certainly no shortage of ways to embrace the season without leaving the five boroughs, sometimes the best fall days are the ones that take you just a little farther from home. If you’re craving crisp autumn air, colorful foliage, charming small-town streets, and a healthy dose of seasonal spookiness, we have just the place for you.

One standout destination just outside the city was recently ranked among the best places in the country to experience fall, and we can’t help but agree. Combining spooky origins with a scenic fall atmosphere and curated seasonal events, Sleepy Hollow, New York has it all for this time of year, including being under an hour from the city.

Unsplash / Richard Hedrick
The Legend & The Leaves: Why USA TODAY Ranked Sleepy Hollow a Top Fall Escape
Sleepy Hollow’s fall magic comes from the fact that it feels like it was made for the season.

The village’s connection to Washington Irving’s The Legend of Sleepy Hollow gives it an unmistakably spooky, storybook atmosphere, while the surrounding Hudson Valley bursts into brilliant autumn color.

Add in seasonal traditions like The Great Jack O’Lantern Blaze at historic Van Cortlandt Manor, where more than 7,000 glowing pumpkins create an elaborate walkthrough display, plus haunted hayrides, street fairs, film festivals, and other fall events, and there’s no shortage of reasons to visit once October rolls around.
With historic landmarks like Lyndhurst Mansion and Philipsburg Manor adding to the scenery, the whole town feels like one giant celebration of everything we love about fall.

Shutterstock / Bri_Adventures
Charming Traditions & Historic Haunts: What to Do in Sleepy Hollow This Fall
Whether you’re looking for historic architecture, scenic walks, or classic Halloween festivities, Sleepy Hollow packs a full itinerary into a cozy footprint:

Marvel at The Great Jack O’Lantern Blaze: Located just minutes away in Croton-on-Hudson, this iconic event features massive glowing sculptures, archways, and displays carved entirely from real pumpkins.

Tour Historic Estates & Manor Grounds: Stroll the grounds of Lyndhurst Mansion, a stunning Gothic Revival estate surrounded by glowing autumn trees, or explore Philipsburg Manor to step back into the 1700s.

Visit the Old Dutch Church & Sleepy Hollow Cemetery: Take a guided evening lantern tour through the historic grounds where Washington Irving himself is buried, alongside famous figures like Andrew Carnegie and William Rockefeller.
Walk the Riverfront & Tarrytown Lighthouse: Take in crisp views of the Hudson River along the Riverwalk leading up to the historic 1883 lighthouse.

Shutterstock / Felix Lipov
Just Up the River: How to Get There from NYC
One of Sleepy Hollow’s best features is how effortlessly accessible it is for city dwellers—no car required.
By Train (Recommended): Hop on the Metro-North Railroad Hudson Line from Grand Central Terminal.
Take an express train to Tarrytown Station (approx. 35–40 minutes), which drops you right at the edge of Main Street’s cozy dining and shopping district.
Alternatively, ride one stop further to Philipse Manor Station for direct access to the Sleepy Hollow riverfront and historic sites.
Tip: Sit on the left side of the train heading north for unbroken, scenic views of the Hudson River all the way up.

By Car: Drive north via I-87 N or the Henry Hudson Parkway/Sprain Brook Parkway N. The 25-mile drive takes roughly 45 to 60 minutes depending on traffic, bringing you right into the heart of Westchester County.
